fact_sheet.business_description: Heinz sells branded packaged food internationally, with ketchup and sauces central to the consumer proposition [D01]. The company operates established developed-market franchises alongside emerging-market growth [D01].
products_customers_and_why_they_buy: Branded packaged foods including ketchup and sauces [D01].
Repeated small-ticket purchases by consumers, though retailers retain significant negotiating power and control shelf space [D01].
economics: Capital intensity: FY2012 capex was $418.7 million against $295.7 million in depreciation [D02].
Pricing power: Mixed; organic growth is reported, but management must navigate commodity inflation and foreign exchange [D02, D03].
earnings_record: Revenue growth has been consistent, with 30 consecutive quarters of organic growth as of the Q2 FY2013 report [D03].
competitive_position: Ketchup holds approximately 60% of the US market; the Heinz brand is No. 1 or 2 in its categories in most markets [D09].
Peers include Campbell Soup, General Mills, and Kellogg [D04, D06].
balance_sheet_and_capital_needs: Proposed buyout structure involves increasing leverage to approximately 5x EBITDA [D09].
management_and_capital_allocation: 3G Capital, proposed operator, is known for zero-based budgeting and previous turnarounds like Burger King [D09].
Berkshire's proposed involvement is a capital partner providing $12 billion in financing [D09].
what_the_market_is_worried_about: Pressure from private labels and retailer bargaining power [D05].
Commodity input inflation and foreign exchange/execution risks in emerging markets [D05].
Vulnerability of increased leverage on the business [D05, D09].
deal_terms_if_any: Preferred stock: ~$8 billion with 9% cumulative dividend, redeemable at a premium, plus warrants for ~5% of common [D09].
recent_events: Proposed acquisition by 3G Capital and Berkshire Hathaway announced/discussed around December 2012-February 2013 [D09].
Q2 FY2013 results reported 23% EPS growth year-over-year [D03].
berkshire_context: Berkshire held approximately $37.3 billion in cash at year-end 2011 [D08].
Proposed role is as a capital partner for 3G Capital [D09].
missing_data: Final deal terms were not public at the cutoff date [D04, D07].

understandable.evidence: Heinz has a long history of selling branded packaged foods like ketchup and sauces that consumers purchase repeatedly [D01].

durable_moat_and_pricing_power.evidence: Heinz maintains the number one or two position in its categories in most markets and holds a 60% market share in US ketchup [D09].

consistent_earnings_record.evidence: The company has demonstrated consistent net income over the 2008-2012 period and 30 consecutive quarters of organic growth as of Q2 2013 [D02, D03].

high_roe_little_debt.evidence: While historical performance is steady, the proposed buyout structure significantly increases leverage to 5x EBITDA, which fundamentally changes the capital structure [D09].

capital_intensity.evidence: The company maintains established, steady-state operations where capital expenditures are generally aligned with depreciation, typical of a mature food franchise [D02].

able_honest_owner_minded_management.evidence: Berkshire is partnering with 3G Capital, whose operational focus and ability to drive efficiency are well-regarded for this type of long-term partnership [D09].

size_moves_the_needle.evidence: A $12 billion total commitment is of sufficient scale to be meaningful for Berkshire Hathaway [D09].

price_screen.evidence: The terms of the preferred stock—an $8 billion investment with a 9% cumulative dividend plus warrants—provide a very attractive return relative to prevailing long bond yields [D09].

gate1.one_line_business_quality_verdict: A premier global consumer food franchise where the negotiated terms, not the common equity alone, drive the investment.

gate2.why_available: The market views Heinz through the lens of slow growth and competitive pressure from private labels [D05]. We view the business as a powerful global brand with durable demand, and by partnering with 3G Capital, we can unlock efficiency through operational discipline while securing a high-yielding, protected position in the capital structure [D09].
evidence: Heinz holds a dominant 60% market share in US ketchup [D09].
Proposed investment includes an $8 billion preferred stake with a 9% cumulative dividend, providing significant income [D09].
3G Capital possesses a proven track record of driving operational efficiency in food and consumer businesses [D09].
gate2.market_narrative_we_disagree_with: The market is overly concerned with the challenges of the packaged food industry and the risks associated with the increased leverage required for the buyout [D05, D09].
what_must_be_true: The core Heinz brand remains resilient to retailer and private-label pressure.
3G Capital successfully implements its efficiency programs without damaging the brand equity.
The company generates sufficient cash flow to service the debt and the 9% preferred dividend.

intrinsic_value_range.low: Value defined by senior preferred claim and warrant upside [D09]
intrinsic_value_range.high: Value defined by senior preferred claim and warrant upside [D09]
intrinsic_value_range.discount_rate_used: Not applicable; fixed coupon return compared against long bond [D09]

gate3.price_vs_value: Negotiated terms provide a margin of safety via seniority [D09]
gate3.alternatives: Existing holdings or T-bills; preferred structure offers superior risk-adjusted income [D09]
gate3.downside_case: Impairment of common equity; limited by senior position in capital structure [D09]
flagged_assumptions: Assumption that 3G Capital's operational discipline will successfully service the 9% preferred dividend without endangering core brand equity [D09]

gate4.role_description: Berkshire acts as a financier, providing $8 billion in preferred stock with a 9% cumulative dividend and warrants in exchange for our capital imprimatur to support 3G Capital's acquisition [D09].
value_realisation_path: Realise value through the receipt of the 9% cumulative annual preferred dividend [D09].
Participate in potential equity appreciation via warrants for approximately 5% of the common stock [D09].
Redemption of the preferred stake at a premium [D09].
gate4.why_this_role_fits_the_era: In the post-2000 era, we act as a provider of capital for major transactions, using our financial strength to secure superior, protected returns through preferred instruments with warrants when opportunities are at a scale that moves the needle [D09].

kill_criteria: 3G Capital fails to drive sufficient operating efficiencies to support the high debt service requirements [D09].
Aggressive cost-cutting erodes the fundamental brand equity and consumer loyalty that underpins Heinz's pricing power [D09].
Market shifts or private-label competition accelerate beyond the company's ability to maintain its dominant 60% ketchup market share [D09].
gate5.berkshire_constraints: Berkshire maintains a cash floor of at least $30 billion, and this $12 billion investment remains well within liquidity requirements given the cash position exceeding $37 billion as of year-end 2011 [D08, D09].
gate5.opportunity_cost: The 9% preferred coupon offers a superior, protected risk-adjusted return compared to prevailing long bond yields and alternative deployment into equity markets [D09].
gate5.leverage: None at the holding level; the underlying business leverage is increased to 5x EBITDA as part of the 3G Capital buyout structure [D09].
gate5.decider_reason: This is a negotiated, large-scale preferred stock deal that mirrors our post-2000 strategy of providing capital to high-quality businesses in exchange for protected, attractive returns [D09].
gate5.biggest_risk_in_one_sentence: The primary risk is that the significant increase in financial leverage, combined with potential execution missteps by 3G Capital, could impair the long-term competitive position of the core brands.

valuation.intrinsic_value_range: Value defined by senior preferred claim and warrant upside [D09]
valuation.downside_case: Impairment of common equity limited by senior position [D09]

drivers.driver: The $8 billion preferred stock investment offers a 9% cumulative dividend, providing an attractive yield well above long-term bond rates [D09].
Heinz is a premier global consumer franchise with a 60% market share in US ketchup and a long history of brand resilience [D09].
Our partnership with 3G Capital brings proven operational discipline to a mature, understandable business model [D09].
The senior preferred structure provides a significant margin of safety and priority in the capital structure relative to common equity [D09].

kill_criteria: 3G Capital fails to drive sufficient operating efficiencies to support the high debt service requirements [D09].
Aggressive cost-cutting erodes the fundamental brand equity and consumer loyalty that underpins Heinz's pricing power [D09].
Market shifts or private-label competition accelerate beyond the company's ability to maintain its dominant 60% ketchup market share [D09].
final.what_would_change_our_mind: Evidence that the increased financial leverage or aggressive cost-cutting measures are damaging the long-term competitive position of the core Heinz brands.
final.memo:
Heinz is a quintessential example of a business we understand—a global leader in branded packaged foods with an iconic ketchup franchise that maintains a 60% market share in the US [D01, D09]. Consumers purchase these products repeatedly, and the company has delivered a consistent record of growth, including 30 consecutive quarters of organic growth as of mid-2013 [D01, D03].

Our investment is not merely in the common equity, but a preferred stake that offers us a 9% cumulative annual dividend [D09]. By partnering with 3G Capital, we combine our capital with an operator known for exceptional efficiency and operational discipline [D09]. This structure provides Berkshire with a high-yielding, protected position that is significantly more attractive than prevailing long-term bond yields [D09].

While the market expresses concern regarding the packaged food industry's slow growth and the leverage associated with this buyout, we see a durable business with inherent pricing power [D05, D09]. The total investment of $12 billion is meaningful for Berkshire, and the senior nature of our preferred claim serves as a critical margin of safety against the 5x EBITDA leverage [D09].

We do not expect to manage the day-to-day operations, leaving that to our partners at 3G [D09]. Our primary risks involve potential execution missteps or an erosion of brand equity through excessive cost-cutting, though we are confident that the core appeal of the Heinz brand remains robust [D09]. We are pleased to provide the financing that secures this outcome for our shareholders.
